items.title: Roy Campanella
items.credit: New York World-Telegram and the Sun staff photographer
items.fact: Roy Campanella (November 19, 1921 – June 26, 1993), nicknamed "Campy", was an American professional baseball player, primarily as a catcher. The Philadelphia native played in the Negro leagues and Mexican League for nine years before entering the minor leagues in 1946.

items.title: Vladimir Guerrero

items.title: Jim Thome

items.title: Michael Jordan
items.fact: Michael Jeffrey Jordan (born February 17, 1963), also known by his initials MJ, is an American businessman, former professional basketball player, and former baseball player. items.credit: The original uploader was Hakandahlstrom at English Wikipedia. Later versions were uploaded by IrisKawling at en.wikipedia.
items.fact: Wayne Douglas Gretzky ( GRET-skee; born January 26, 1961) is a Canadian former professional ice hockey player and head coach. He played 20 seasons in the National Hockey League (NHL) for four teams from 1979 to 1999.

items.title: Mario Lemieux
items.fact: Mario Lemieux is a Canadian former professional ice hockey player. He played parts of 17 seasons in the National Hockey League (NHL) for the Pittsburgh Penguins between 1984 and 2005, and he assumed ownership of the franchise in 1999.

items.title: Alexander Ovechkin
items.fact: Alexander Mikhailovich Ovechkin is a Russian professional ice hockey player who is a left winger and captain for the Washington Capitals of the National Hockey League (NHL).
items.group: a Russian professional ice hockey player

items.title: Vladislav Tretiak
items.fact: Vladislav Aleksandrovich Tretiak MP is a Russian former goaltender for the Soviet Union national ice hockey team. He was inducted into the inaugural class of the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) Hall of Fame in 1997.

items.title: Gordie Howe
items.fact: Gordon Howe (March 31, 1928 – June 10, 2016) was a Canadian professional ice hockey player. From 1946 to 1980, he played 26 seasons in the National Hockey League (NHL) and six seasons in the World Hockey Association (WHA); his first 25 seasons were spent with the Detroit Red Wings.
items.group: a Canadian professional ice hockey player

items.title: Sidney Crosby
items.fact: Sidney Patrick Crosby (born August 7, 1987) is a Canadian professional ice hockey player who is a centre and captain for the Pittsburgh Penguins of the National Hockey League (NHL). Nicknamed "Sid the Kid" and dubbed "The Next One", he was selected first overall by the Penguins in the 2005 NHL entry draft.
items.group: a Canadian professional ice hockey player

items.title: Jaromír Jágr
items.fact: Jaromír Jágr is a Czech professional ice hockey player who is a right winger and owner of Rytíři Kladno of the Czech Extraliga (ELH).
items.group: a Czech professional ice hockey player

items.title: Bobby Hull
items.fact: Robert Marvin Hull (January 3, 1939 – January 30, 2023) was a Canadian professional ice hockey player who is widely regarded as one of the greatest players of all time. His blond hair, skating speed, end-to-end rushes, and ability to shoot the puck at very high velocity all earned him the nickname "the Golden Jet".
items.group: a Canadian professional ice hockey player

items.title: Bobby Orr
items.fact: Robert Gordon Orr (born March 20, 1948) is a Canadian former professional ice hockey player who is widely acknowledged as one of the greatest players of all time. Orr used his skating speed, scoring, and play-making abilities to revolutionize the position of defenceman.
items.group: a Canadian former professional ice hockey player

items.title: Dominik Hašek
items.fact: Dominik Hašek is a Czech former professional ice hockey player who was a goaltender for 16 seasons in the National Hockey League (NHL), mostly for the Buffalo Sabres.

items.title: Mark Messier
items.fact: Mark John Douglas Messier (born January 18; 1961) is a Canadian former professional ice hockey forward. His playing career in the National Hockey League (NHL) lasted 25 seasons (1979–2004) with the Edmonton Oilers, New York Rangers and Vancouver Canucks.
items.group: a Canadian former professional ice hockey forward

items.title: Henrik Sedin
items.fact: Henrik Lars Sedin (seh-DEEN; born 26 September 1980) is a Swedish ice hockey executive and former centre who played his entire 17-season National Hockey League (NHL) career with the Vancouver Canucks from 2000 to 2018. He additionally served as the Canucks' captain from 2010 until his retirement.
items.group: a Swedish ice hockey executive and former centre

items.group: a Canadian professional ice hockey coach

items.title: Steve Yzerman
items.fact: Stephen Gregory Yzerman is a Canadian former professional hockey player who is currently a senior advisor for the Detroit Red Wings. A Detroit sports icon and a member of the Hockey Hall of Fame, Yzerman played his entire 22-season career with the Red Wings.

items.title: Nicklas Lidström

items.title: David Beckham
items.fact: Sir David Robert Joseph Beckham is an English former professional footballer, the president and co-owner of Inter Miami CF and co-owner of Salford City F.C.. Primarily a right midfielder and known for his range of passing, crossing ability and set-piece taking, Beckham is considered one of the best players of his generation and one of the greatest set-piece specialists of all time.

items.title: Kylian Mbappé
items.fact: Kylian Mbappé Lottin (born 20 December 1998) is a French professional footballer who plays as a forward for La Liga club Real Madrid and captains the France national team. Widely regarded as one of the best players in the world, he is known for his pace, dribbling, and finishing.

items.title: Johan Cruyff

items.title: Zlatan Ibrahimović

items.title: Novak Djokovic
items.fact: Novak Djokovic (born 22 May 1987) is a Serbian professional tennis player. He has been ranked as the world No. 1 in men's singles by the Association of Tennis Professionals (ATP) for a record 428 weeks, finished as the year-end No. 1 a record eight times, and has been ranked No. 1 at least once in a year for a record 13 different years.

items.title: Serena Williams
items.fact: Serena Jameka Williams (born September 26, 1981) is an American professional tennis player. She was ranked as the world No. 1 in women's singles by the Women's Tennis Association (WTA) for 319 weeks (third-most of all time), and finished as the year-end No. 1 five times.
items.group: an American professional tennis player

items.title: Maria Sharapova

items.fact: Stefanie Maria Graf, known professionally as Steffi Graf and preferring to be called Stefanie since 2001, is a German former professional tennis player. items.title: Martina Hingis
items.fact: Martina Hingis (born 30 September 1980) is a Swiss former professional tennis player. items.group: a Swiss former professional tennis player

items.title: Björn Borg
items.fact: Björn Rune Borg is a Swedish former professional tennis player. He was ranked as the world No. 1 in men's singles by the Association of Tennis Professionals (ATP) for 109 weeks.
items.group: a Swedish former professional tennis player

items.title: Boris Becker
items.fact: Boris Franz Becker is a German former professional tennis player, tennis coach and a commentator. He was ranked as the world No. 1 in men's singles by the Association of Tennis Professionals (ATP).
items.group: a German former professional tennis player

items.title: John McEnroe
items.fact: John Patrick McEnroe Jr. (born February 16, 1959) is an American former professional tennis player.
items.group: an American former professional tennis player

items.title: Kim Clijsters
items.fact: Kim Antonie Lode Clijsters is a Belgian former professional tennis player. She was ranked as the world No. 1 in women's singles by the Women's Tennis Association (WTA) for 20 weeks, and as the world No. 1 in women's doubles for 4 weeks, having held both rankings simultaneously in 2003.
items.group: a Belgian former professional tennis player

items.title: Amélie Mauresmo
items.fact: Amélie Simone Mauresmo is a French former professional tennis player, tennis coach, and tournament director. She was ranked as the world No. 1 in women's singles by the Women's Tennis Association (WTA) for 39 weeks.
items.group: a French former professional tennis player

items.title: Andy Roddick
items.fact: Andrew Stephen Roddick (born August 30, 1982) is an American former professional tennis player. He was ranked as the world No. 1 in men's singles by the Association of Tennis Professionals (ATP) for 13 weeks, including as the year-end No. 1 in 2003.
items.group: an American former professional tennis player

items.title: Monica Seles
items.credit: Kingkongphoto & www.celebrity-photos.com from Laurel Maryland, USA
items.fact: Monica Seles (born December 2, 1973) is a former professional tennis player who represented Yugoslavia and the United States. She was ranked as the world No. 1 in women's singles by the WTA for 178 weeks (sixth-most of all time), and finished as the year-end No. 1 three times.
items.group: a former professional tennis player

items.title: Tiger Woods
items.credit: The White House from Washington, DC
items.fact: Eldrick Tont "Tiger" Woods (born December 30, 1975) is an American professional golfer. He is widely regarded as one of the greatest golfers of all time and as one of the most famous athletes in modern history.
items.group: an American professional golfer

items.title: Annika Sörenstam
items.fact: Annika Charlotta Sörenstam is a Swedish and American professional golfer regarded as one of the best female golfers in history.

items.title: Rory McIlroy
items.fact: Rory Daniel McIlroy (born 4 May 1989) is a Northern Irish professional golfer who plays on the PGA Tour and the European Tour. He is a former world number one in the Official World Golf Ranking and has spent over 100 weeks in that position during his career.
items.group: a Northern Irish professional golfer

items.title: Gary Player
items.fact: Gary James Player (born 1 November 1935) is a South African retired professional golfer who is widely considered to be one of the greatest golfers of all time. Player won over 160 professional tournaments across six continents, including nine major championships.
items.group: a South African retired professional golfer

items.title: Lee Trevino
items.fact: Lee Buck Trevino (born December 1, 1939) is an American retired professional golfer who is regarded as one of the greatest players in golf history. He was inducted to the World Golf Hall of Fame in 1981.
items.group: an American retired professional golfer

items.title: Justin Rose
items.fact: Justin Peter Rose (born 30 July 1980) is an English professional golfer who plays on the PGA Tour and the European Tour. He is a former world number one in the Official World Golf Ranking.
items.group: an English professional golfer

items.title: Michelle Wie West
items.credit: Keith Allison from Hanover, MD, USA
items.fact: Michelle Sung Wie West (née Wie; born October 11, 1989) is an American professional golfer who plays on the LPGA Tour. At age 10, she became the youngest player to qualify for a USGA amateur championship.
items.group: an American professional golfer

items.title: Ernie Els
items.fact: Theodore Ernest Els (born 17 October 1969) is a South African professional golfer. A former World No. 1, he is nicknamed "The Big Easy" due to his physical stature along with his fluid golf swing.
items.group: a South African professional golfer

items.title: Greg Norman
items.fact: Gregory John Norman (born 10 February 1955) is an Australian retired professional golfer who spent 331 weeks as world number one in the 1980s and 1990s. He won 88 professional tournaments, including 20 PGA Tour tournaments and two majors: The Open Championship in 1986 and 1993.
items.group: an Australian retired professional golfer

items.title: Sam Snead
items.fact: Samuel Jackson Snead ( SNEED; May 27, 1912 – May 23, 2002) was an American professional golfer who was one of the top players in the world for the better part of four decades (having won PGA of America and Senior PGA Tour events over six decades) and widely regarded as one of the greatest players of all time.
items.group: an American professional golfer

items.title: Bernhard Langer
items.fact: Bernhard Langer is a German professional golfer. He is a two-time Masters champion and was one of the world's leading golfers throughout the 1980s and 1990s. In 1986, he became the sport's first number one ranked player following the creation of the Sony Ranking (now the Official World Golf Ranking).
items.group: a German professional golfer

items.title: Lorena Ochoa
items.fact: Lorena Ochoa Reyes is a Mexican professional golfer. She played on the U.S.-based LPGA Tour from 2003 to 2010.
items.group: a Mexican professional golfer

items.title: Muhammad Ali
items.fact: Muhammad Ali ( ah-LEE; born Cassius Marcellus Clay Jr.; January 17, 1942 – June 3, 2016) was an American professional boxer and activist. A global cultural icon, widely known by the nickname "the Greatest", he is often regarded as the greatest heavyweight boxer of all time.
items.group: an American professional boxer and activist

items.title: Mike Tyson
items.fact: Michael Gerard Tyson (born June 30, 1966) is an American former professional boxer who competed between 1985 and 2024.
items.group: an American former professional boxer

items.title: Joe Frazier
items.credit: Bill Apter or David Lee Waite
items.fact: Joseph William Frazier (January 12, 1944 – November 7, 2011) was an American professional boxer who competed from 1965 to 1981. Nicknamed "Smokin’ Joe”, he was known for his strength, durability, formidable left hand, and relentless pressure fighting style.
items.group: an American professional boxer

items.title: Manny Pacquiao
items.credit: SC Ryan A on Picasa Web Albums
items.fact: Emmanuel Dapidran Pacquiao Sr. is a Filipino professional boxer and former politician.
items.group: a Filipino professional boxer and former politician

items.title: George Foreman
items.credit: Bert Verhoeff, Nationaal Archief, Den Haag, Rijksfotoarchief: Fotocollectie Algemeen Nederlands Fotopersbureau (ANEFO), 1945-1989 - negatief
items.fact: George Edward Foreman (January 10, 1949 – March 21, 2025) was an American professional boxer, businessman, minister, and author. In boxing, he competed between 1967 and 1997, and was nicknamed "Big George".
items.group: an American professional boxer

items.title: Floyd Mayweather
items.credit: DEWALT POWER TOOLS FIGHT NIGHT CLUB 2010
items.fact: Floyd Joy Mayweather Jr. (né Sinclair; born February 24, 1977) is an American professional boxer and boxing promoter.
items.group: an American professional boxer and boxing promoter

items.title: Joe Louis
items.fact: Joseph Louis Barrow (May 13, 1914 – April 12, 1981) was an American professional boxer who competed from 1934 to 1951. Nicknamed "the Brown Bomber", Louis is widely regarded as one of the greatest and most influential boxers of all time.
items.group: an American professional boxer

items.title: Rocky Marciano
items.fact: Rocco Francis Marchegiano, better known as Rocky Marciano, was an American professional boxer who competed from 1947 to 1955.
items.group: an American professional boxer

items.title: Wladimir Klitschko
items.fact: Wladimir Klitschko (born 25 March 1976) is a Ukrainian former professional boxer who competed from 1996 to 2017. He held multiple heavyweight world championships between 2000 and 2015, including unified titles between 2008 and 2015.
items.group: an Ukrainian former professional boxer

items.title: Sugar Ray Robinson
items.fact: Sugar Ray Robinson (born Walker Smith Jr.; May 3, 1921 – April 12, 1989) was an American professional boxer who competed from 1940 to 1965. He was inducted into the International Boxing Hall of Fame in 1990.
items.group: an American professional boxer

items.title: Evander Holyfield
items.fact: Evander Holyfield (born October 19, 1962) is an American former professional boxer who competed between 1984 and 2011.
items.group: an American former professional boxer

items.title: Jack Dempsey
items.fact: William Harrison "Jack" Dempsey (June 24, 1895 – May 31, 1983), nicknamed Kid Blackie and The Manassa Mauler, was an American boxer who competed from 1914 to 1927, and was world heavyweight champion from 1919 to 1926.
items.group: an American boxer

items.title: Lennox Lewis
items.fact: Lennox Claudius Lewis (born 2 September 1965) is a boxing commentator and former professional boxer who competed in the heavyweight division from 1989 to 2003. He was a three-time world champion, a two-time lineal champion, and held the undisputed championship.
items.group: a boxing commentator and former professional boxer

items.title: Max Schmeling
items.credit: Wm. C. Greene - New York World-Telegram and the Sun
items.fact: Maximilian "Max" Adolph Otto Siegfried Schmeling was a German boxer who was heavyweight champion of the world between 1930 and 1932. His two fights with Joe Louis in 1936 and 1938 were worldwide cultural events because of their national associations.
items.group: a German boxer
